items.title: iMac G3
items.line: Apple unveiled the iMac on 6 May 1998 and shipped it on 15 August. Jony Ive's Bondi Blue case dropped the floppy drive for USB, and 800,000 sold in 20 weeks.

items.title: France wins the World Cup
items.line: France beat Brazil 3-0 on 12 July 1998 at the Stade de France. Zidane scored twice with headers, and about 1.5 million fans filled the Champs-Élysées.

items.title: Furby
items.line: Furby went on sale on 2 October 1998 for about $35. Tiger Electronics sold 1.8 million that year and 14 million in 1999, and each one spoke Furbish until it picked up English.

items.title: Ocarina of Time
items.line: Ocarina of Time reached Japan on 21 November 1998 and North America two days later. It holds a 99 on Metacritic from 22 reviews and has sold over seven million copies.

items.title: Google
items.line: Larry Page and Sergey Brin founded Google on 4 September 1998 in Menlo Park, working from Susan Wojcicki's garage on a $100,000 cheque from Andy Bechtolsheim.

items.title: Sex and the City
items.line: Sex and the City premiered on HBO on 6 June 1998. Darren Star adapted Candace Bushnell's newspaper column, and the show ran 94 episodes over six seasons.

items.title: Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?
items.line: Chris Tarrant started hosting Who Wants to Be a Millionaire? on ITV on 4 September 1998. The all-time audience peak was 19.2 million, on 7 March 1999.
